title: Git Refs and HEAD
description: Learn how Git references work, what HEAD means, and how to manipulate refs directly.

data.text: Git references (refs) are human-friendly pointers to commits stored as plain text files in the .git directory. Branches, tags, and HEAD are all refs. Understanding how refs work is essential for recovering from history rewrites and writing Git automation.

data.title: Refs are just files
data.text: Every ref is stored as a plain text file in .git/refs/. You can read them with cat, echo into them, or delete them. This makes Git's reference system simple to inspect and script against.
Local branches live in .git/refs/heads/ and tags in .git/refs/tags/. Each file contains the 40-character SHA-1 of the commit it points to. Remote-tracking branches live in .git/refs/remotes/origin/.

data.title: Inspect and manipulate refs
data.code:
# Read a branch ref directly
cat .git/refs/heads/main

# See all refs (branches, tags, remotes)
git for-each-ref

# See only branches
git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short)' refs/heads/

# List all tags
git tag

data.text: HEAD is a symbolic ref that points to the currently checked-out branch. In detached HEAD state, HEAD points directly to a commit SHA instead of a branch. Use git switch or git checkout to move between branches or enter detached state.

data.title: Check where HEAD points
data.code:
# See the symbolic target of HEAD
git symbolic-ref HEAD

# In detached HEAD, symbolic-ref fails — use this instead
git rev-parse HEAD

# Enter detached HEAD
git checkout abc1234
# Return to a branch
git switch main

data.title: Detached HEAD is not broken
data.text: Detached HEAD is perfectly valid for temporary exploration. Just avoid making permanent commits there — create a branch first if you intend to keep your work.

Every time a ref moves, Git records the change in a reflog. HEAD reflog entries look like HEAD@{n} and branch reflogs look like feature/auth@{n}. Reflogs expire after 90 days by default and are the primary recovery tool after rebases and resets.

data.title: Use the reflog to recover
data.code:
# View HEAD reflog
git reflog

# Recover a branch to a lost commit
git branch recovery HEAD@{5}

# Reset HEAD to a previous state
git reset --hard HEAD@{2}

# View reflog for a specific branch
git reflog show feature/auth

data.text: While you normally use git branch and git tag, Git provides low-level commands for ref manipulation. git update-ref is the safe way to update a ref — it checks that the old value matches before writing.

data.title: Create and delete refs with update-ref
data.code:
# Safely update a ref (fails if old value does not match)
git update-ref refs/heads/recovery abc1234

# Delete a ref safely
git update-ref -d refs/heads/old-branch

# Verify a ref before deleting
git show-ref --verify refs/heads/old-branch

items.question: What happens to the reflog when I delete a branch?
items.answer: The branch reflog is deleted, but the HEAD reflog still records the checkout and any subsequent actions. You can still recover lost commits through HEAD@{n} entries.

items.question: Are reflogs shared across clones?
items.answer: No. Reflogs are entirely local to each clone. They are never pushed or pulled. You cannot recover commits from reflogs on another developer's machine.

items.question: How can I prevent reflog entries from expiring?
items.answer: Use git config --global gc.reflogExpire never to keep entries indefinitely. This is not recommended for normal use, but can be useful for critical branches.

items.question: What is the difference between a symbolic ref and a direct ref?
items.answer: A direct ref points straight to a commit SHA. A symbolic ref points to another ref name. HEAD is usually symbolic (pointing to refs/heads/main). Use git symbolic-ref to check.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Branches, tags, and HEAD are all refs — plain-text files in .git/
HEAD is a symbolic ref to the current branch, or a direct SHA in detached state
The reflog records every ref movement and is your primary recovery tool
git update-ref is the safe way to manipulate refs programmatically
Reflogs are local-only and expire after 90 days by default
